messages:
leo: Heads up — staging-edge-1 started throwing a bunch of 502/504s around 10:05. Model pulls and health-checks failing for several GPU nodes. CloudWatch shows a sharp spike in NAT active connections from that subnet.
anya: saw that too, alert from infra-bot pushed at 10:06. Pods reporting connection resets when contacting S3/model-registry.
infra-bot: [ALERT] outbound-conn-high on subnet:staging-edge-1 - ActiveConnections increased from 1.2k -> 58k in 3m.
chris: can someone run ss -s and check TIME_WAIT / ephemeral allocation? my guess is source-port exhaustion behind a single SNAT IP.
leo: ran quick checks on one affected node: lots of TIME_WAIT, local ports near 61k. netstat output snippet: 
```
$ ss -tn state TIME-WAIT sport :1024-65535 | wc -l
~ 42k
$ sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768 60999
```
anya: ah that's why — our local range ends at 60999 which is lower than full ephemeral range. But even if extended we still hit single-EIP limit when many pods open short-lived outbound connections.
ops-sre: reminder: AWS NAT gateway uses a single EIP per gateway and per-source-ip you only get ~64k ports. With 1 EIP the practical SNAT ports are ~61000 minus reserved, and conntrack and TIME_WAIT reduce usable. we were seeing ~58k active — very close.
chris: immediate mitigations: 1) switch model pullers to use node-local cache / registry mirror (imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent) 2) deploy short-lived egress-proxy DaemonSet to multiplex connections with keepalives 3) spin up a second NAT gateway in the AZ and add route table entries to split egress by subnet.
anya: started a canary: registry-mirror on 2 nodes and imagePullPolicy change for model-init job in staging. Rolling now.
leo: also tried sysctl tweaks on a node (temporarily) to reclaim ports quicker: 
```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_recycle=0  # deprecated, left off
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='10240 65535'
```
chris: careful with tcp_tw_reuse; safe for client-only but monitor for weirdness. conntrack table pressure will still be the limiter. bumping conntrack_max might help short-term.
ops-sre: opened an infra ticket to provision a second NAT gateway + EIP per staging AZ. Also evaluating a VPC egress fleet (HAproxy) that can present multiple source IPs per node using multiple ENIs.
anya: long term: we should prefer egress pooling (sidecar or dedicated pool) + registry mirrors close to the clusters. For model pulls specifically, consider an internal model cache layer (s3 proxy with keepalive) so nodes don't open bursts.
leo: noted root cause for postmortem: single-SNAT-IP exhaustion due to high fanout short-lived connections from parallel model pull jobs + restrictive ip_local_port_range.
chris: action items: @anya roll out mirror + imagePullPolicy canary (in progress). @ops-sre provision second NAT gw and update route table (ticket #INF-4821). @leo run conntrack and port-range audit across all AZs and propose node sysctl baseline. I'll help test egress-proxy PoC.
ops-sre: will update ticket with ETA. if we see staging recovery after canary, we'll promote to prod scheduling.
leo: one-off note — adding keepalive/connection-pooling to the model downloader code reduced new outbound sockets by ~85% in a short test. recommend that change in codepath too.
anya: thumbs up. will include in the follow-up PR. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [INFO] ticket INF-4821 created by ops-sre for multi-eip-egress and NAT gw addition.
chris: thanks — will coordinate a brief postmortem doc after we validate mitigations.
leo: closing thread for now; will re-open if we see another surge.
